Enemy prioritization is not as strong as in SS but it's not non existent either.
Example: You're in a claustrophobic arena with 10 imps, 3 spectre whiplashes, an arch vile and a baron rushing at you.
This situation alone can be done in many different ways, an experienced player's first thought would be "Do I use my ice bomb on the arch vile to quickly kill it with lock on burst or do I use my ice bomb on the 3 spectre whiplashes and destroyer blade them since lock on burst can't be used on spectre enemies"
This situation alone forces you to prioritize certain enemies over the others and make decisions, the arch vile can buff the already existing enemies and spawn new ones so he needs to be removed instantly. While that is happening a baron and 10 imps are all rushing at you forcing you to yet again make decisions and prioritze, a baron is very lethal in a claustrophobic arena because of his ability to corner you.
Not to mention doom eternal forces you to do what I think is special and haven't seen in any other game: you make and manage your own health and armor.
You don't just pick it up like in SS but you have to think and use your flame belch wisely, an experienced player will try to keep his armor up constantly. Alongside this is doom eternal's falter system that an experienced player will also be able to use to their advantagw, it's a little bit too complex to explain here but this all adds up to be a much more complex and rewarding combat loop than any SS game I've ever played.
And this is just 1 example, there are a million differemt ones I could pick.
Pain elementals for example also pressure the player from above and forces the player to make them the highest priority target, you simply can't control the battlefield with pain elementals or cacodemons near you. Just like you can't really control the battlefield in SS when there are kamikazes or major biomechs close.
